name: Browser extension
summary: A browser extension that sends chosen github.com pages (pull requests, issues, repositories, profiles) to the same page in DiffKit. The dashboard offers it when it is missing.

flow.label: github.com page
flow.note: The user opens a GitHub link from somewhere other than GitHub or DiffKit.

flow.label: Redirect script
flow.note: Skips visits that came from GitHub or DiffKit, then looks for an enabled matching rule.

flow.label: Rule storage
flow.note: Eight default rules live in browser sync storage and can be toggled or edited.

flow.label: DiffKit page
flow.note: The browser lands on the matching route, for example /owner/repo/pull/12.

flow.label: Presence marker
flow.note: Sets data-diffkit-extension=1 on <html> so the app knows the extension is installed.

flow.label: Install prompt
flow.note: Shown in the bottom bar on desktop when the marker is missing.

features.name: Redirect rules
features.summary: Eight default rules: home, pulls, issues, repo overview, pull request, PR changes to the review page, issue and profile. Each is a regex or an exact URL.

entry.role: First enabled rule that matches a URL
Runs on github.com at document start

features.name: Popup toggles
features.summary: The toolbar popup has a master switch and one toggle per rule, so redirects can be paused without losing the per-rule choices.

features.name: Rule editor
features.summary: The options page shows the rules as JSON, validates them on save and can restore the defaults.

features.name: Extension detection
features.summary: Page code cannot see the extension directly, so a content script marks <html> with a data attribute and the app reads it.

entry.role: Sets the attribute on DiffKit origins

features.name: Install prompt
features.summary: A small chip links to the Chrome Web Store or Firefox Add-ons depending on the browser. Dismissing it hides it for 30 days.

entry.role: The chip in the bottom bar
Picks the store by user agent

features.name: Settings card
features.summary: The settings page has a Browser extension card that shows whether the extension is installed and links to the store when it is not.

features.name: GitHub link mapping
features.summary: Inside the app, github.com links in comments open the matching DiffKit route. A palette command does the reverse and opens the current page on GitHub.

entryPoints.role: Which script runs on which site
How the dashboard knows it is installed

goodParts: No build step and no dependencies: plain Manifest V3 scripts around one shared module, with Firefox settings in the same manifest.json.
The dashboard-side link mapping is tested: github-links.test.ts and github-current-url.test.ts.
watch: Redirect targets and the presence check are fixed to diff-kit.com and localhost:3000 (shared.js, dashboard-presence.js); a self-hosted domain is never detected.
No tests cover the extension's rule matching; extensions/diffkit-redirect has no test files and no package.json.
Default rules redirect /pull/N and /pull/N/changes only; /pull/N/files and /pull/N/commits stay on GitHub (shared.js:63-87).
